definitions.definition: Ttor = reals/(2*pi*integers), with normalized measure dx/(2*pi); spatial products and integrals are on this domain.
For an integrable periodic f, Fourier(f)(k)=hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; the transform extends to distributions by duality.

For every real s, H^s(Ttor) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). Negative spaces are interpreted as distributions. Homogeneous norms on zero-mean distributions are ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. Real means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0.

L2=H^0(Ttor), with ||f||_2^2=(2*pi)^(-1) integral |f|^2 dx. More generally L^p uses the same normalized measure; L^infinity is essential supremum. Sequence ell^2 uses counting measure on Z (or Z\{0} when specified). Time suprema use continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema.

definitions.type: Airy group indexed by real time
definitions.definition: S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3) hat f(k).
P0(f)=hat f(0), identified with a constant function.
Pnz=I-P0, denoted P in the supplied proof. Fourier projections P_leq(N) and P_gt(N) retain |k|<=N and |k|>N respectively, for N>=0.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1) has Fourier multiplier (i*k)^(-1) at nonzero integer k and zero at k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2 is denoted D^(-2).

definitions.type: quadratic update family for positive timestep
definitions.definition: For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L2, Ftau(f)=(1/6)*Pnz[(S_tau Dinv f)^2]-(1/6)*S_tau Pnz[(Dinv f)^2].

definitions.type: cubic update family for positive timestep
definitions.definition: For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L2, Htau(f)=(1/3)*Pnz[(S_tau Dinv f)*Dinv Ftau(f)]+(tau/9)*(S_tau Dinv f)*P0(f^2)-(1/54)*[S_(tau-s) Dinv[(S_s Dinv f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)-(1/(27*tau))*[S_(tau-s) Dinv2[(S_(s-tau) Dinv2 Ftau(f))*(S_s Dinv f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau). Brackets mean the value at tau minus the value at zero. All products are spatial products.

Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+Ftau(f)+Htau(f). Given mean-zero u0 in L2 and an integer L>=1, set tau=T/L, t_n=n*tau, u^0=u0 and u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n) for 0<=n<L; write v^n=S_(-t_n)u^n. There is no spatial cutoff.

KdV is u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)*partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u0. An exact solution on [0,T] with H^gamma data means the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma(Ttor)) distributional solution obtained by smooth approximation. This describes the convention and asserts no existence. For such a solution write v(t)=S_(-t)u(t), and M=1+sup_[0,T]||v(t)||_(H^gamma).
For tau>0 and real alpha,beta, M_tau g=tau^(-1) integral_0^tau g(s) ds and eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).

definitions.type: averaged cubic trilinear Fourier family, initially on polynomials
definitions.definition: For tau>0, t0 real, and mean-zero polynomial inputs f1,f2,f3, define Remainder_(t0,tau)(f1,f2,f3) to have zero mean and, for k!=0, Fourier coefficient -tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t0*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f1(a)*hat f2(b)*hat f3(c), where p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p and Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. Its bounded extensions will be proved; R^n_(2,tau) means t0=t_n.
Bop_t(f,g)=S_(-t)*partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic functions and by distributional product for L2 inputs.
Jop_t(f,g)=S_(-t) Pnz[(S_t Dinv f)(S_t Dinv g)].

For a time interval I=[a,b], Cop_I(f,g,h)=integral_a^b S_(-t) Pnz{Pnz[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))} dt. Initially this is defined for smooth inputs; the continuous extensions in the source estimates are meant when used for rough inputs.
pstar=23/14.

For an interval I of length at most one, ||f||_X(I)=||f||_(L^infinity(I;L2))+||partial_t f||_(L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar))). Derivatives are distributional time derivatives, with their essential-supremum norms.

For a grid start t_n=n*tau, tau>0, and time-independent mean-zero w, Stage_n(t;w)=(1/2) integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(w,w) ds for t in [t_n,t_n+tau]. The associated bilinear stage has w1,w2 in its two slots.

For smooth mean-zero initial data and tau=T/L>0, on I_n=[t_n,t_(n+1)] put f_n=v^n, F_n(t)=Stage_n(t;f_n), z_n(t)=f_n+F_n(t), C_n(t)=integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(f_n,F_n(s)) ds, Q_n(t)=(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(F_n(s),F_n(s)) ds, W_n=Q_n(t_(n+1))+Remainder_(t_n,tau)(f_n,f_n,f_n), V(t)=f_n+F_n(t)+C_n(t)+Q_n(t)-(t-t_n)*W_n/tau, and Y_n(t)=V(t)-z_n(t). Put rho_n(t)=-integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(Y_n,z_n) ds-(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(Y_n,Y_n) ds-(t-t_n)*W_n/tau. Define Rres(0)=0 and concatenate rho_n: Rres(t)=sum_(j<n)rho_j(t_(j+1))+rho_n(t) on I_n. For an exact twisted solution v, set e=v-V, delta_n=||f_n-v(t_n)||_2, q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n. V is initially stepwise defined; continuity is a proved assertion. The per-step formulas define a tuple of functions for any prescribed smooth mean-zero step state f_n, step start n*tau and positive tau, independently of whether f_n comes from a full trajectory. In that local use, any comparison state w may replace v(t_n) in delta_n=||f_n-w||_2 and q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n. Full concatenation, V on the whole time interval and e=v-V concern a full numerical trajectory and an exact solution as specified above.

inputs.statement: There is A=A(T,gamma,R)<infinity such that every real mean-zero initial datum f0 in H^gamma with ||f0||_(H^gamma)<=R has a unique exact KdV solution in the convention D012 and sup_[0,T]||u(t)||_(H^gamma)<=A. Smooth initial data give smooth solutions, with the same H^gamma bound. Thus the twisted v=S_(-t)u obeys M<=1+A uniformly on this ball. For any B>0, two real mean-zero initial L2 data with norm sum <=B have flows satisfying sup_[0,T]||u-tilde u||_2<=C(T,B)||u0-tilde u0||_2. In particular real mean-zero Fourier polynomial approximations to H^gamma data converge in C([0,T];L2) to this solution.

S_t is an isometry on every H^s and preserves real functions and zero mean; Fourier projections contract these norms. For mean-zero L2 inputs, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2, ||Bop_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||Jop_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2 and ||Jop_t(A,B)||_2<=C||Dinv A||_2||B||_2, uniformly in t. For arbitrary L2 F,G, ||Dinv Pnz(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2. For mean-zero A, ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2. H^1 embeds continuously into L^infinity and satisfies ||AB||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||B||_(H^1). For time-smooth spatially smooth mean-zero f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b Bop_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[Jop_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[Jop_t(f',g)+Jop_t(f,g')]dt. Also Jop is symmetric and integral_I Jop_t(Bop_t(f,g),h)dt=Cop_I(f,g,h). These identities hold piecewise in time and add across adjoining steps with their common endpoints. For every fixed tau>0, Ftau:L2_zero->H^1 and Psi_tau:L2_zero->L2_zero are continuous polynomial maps, preserve reality, and map smooth data to smooth data; all finite iterates are therefore well defined and continuous in L2.

inputs.statement: There exist C>0 and tau0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that for every smooth real mean-zero u0 with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every integer L>=1, tau=T/L<=tau0, the interpolation D023 satisfies sup_[0,T]||S_(-t)u(t)-V(t)||_2<=C tau^gamma. Hence max_(0<=n<=L)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_2<=C tau^gamma for all these smooth data, uniformly in all higher Sobolev norms and Fourier support.

output.statement: There exist positive constants C and tau0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(Ttor) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0, the exact KdV solution in D012 exists and the unmodified unfiltered scheme D009–D011 is well defined and satisfies max_(0<=n<=L)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_(L2)<=C*tau^gamma. These constants are uniform on the entire initial-data ball, all permitted timesteps, and all Fourier supports, with the domain, normalized measure, Fourier/Sobolev conventions, Airy group, projections, inverse derivatives and full Ftau,Htau formula fixed in D001–D012.

locals.declaration: Fix arbitrary u0 and assume L1: u0 is real mean-zero in H^gamma with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R.
Fix arbitrary positive integer Lsteps; set tau=T/Lsteps and assume tau<=tau0 from N013.
Define u0m=P_leq(m)u0, m a positive integer.
Take the exact solution for u0 supplied by N001.
For each u0m take its smooth exact solution supplied by N001.
Use the uniform positive error constant C provided by N013, independent of datum and step size.
Use the positive uniform threshold tau0 provided by N013.
Set tau=T/Lsteps with tau<=tau0, as stipulated for the permitted integer Lsteps.

argument.text: H001–H003 give the target parameter ranges. Take C,tau0 from N013, which were chosen before fixing the datum or the step size. Fix u0 under L1 and arbitrary positive integer Lsteps with tau=T/Lsteps<=tau0. Define u0m=P_leq(m)u0. Fourier truncation preserves reality and zero mean, gives ||u0m||_(H^gamma)<=R, and u0m->u0 in H^gamma and L2 because the tails of the defining positive square sum tend to zero. N001 supplies their smooth exact solutions and the unique limiting solution, with a common bound depending only on T,gamma,R. Its L2 Lipschitz estimate at B=2R gives sup_[0,T]||uapprox_m-uexact||_2<=C(T,2R)||u0m-u0||_2->0.

produces.statement: Under L1, the Fourier polynomial data stay in the same H^gamma ball and their exact flows converge uniformly in time in L2 to uexact.

argument.text: For this fixed tau>0, N005 proves continuity of Psi_tau on mean-zero L2 and preservation of real mean-zero functions. Induction over the finite number Lsteps of updates therefore gives u_m^n->u^n in L2 for each n=0,...,Lsteps, starting from u0m->u0. In particular the unmodified scheme is defined for u0 itself; no Fourier cutoff is introduced. All coefficients, including tau^(-1), remain finite in this fixed-timestep limit. N013 applies to every smooth u0m with precisely the same C,tau0. At each grid point combine convergence of the exact and numerical terms; by continuity of the norm its limit satisfies ||uexact(n*tau)-u^n||_2<=C*tau^gamma. The maximum over the finite set of Lsteps+1 points has the same bound (equivalently finite maxima commute with these limits).

produces.statement: Under L1 the full grid error for u0 and this arbitrary permitted Lsteps is <=C tau^gamma, with C,tau0 independent of u0 and Lsteps.

argument.text: Discharge L1, retaining every real, mean-zero, H^gamma and radius condition in the universal assertion. Quantify over u0 and Lsteps, renaming Lsteps to L. The constants remain the uniform constants already fixed in S001, independent of approximation support, datum and timestep. D001–D012 are exactly the selected domain, normalized norms, solution convention and fixed scheme; the final bound is therefore the complete selected Theorem 1.
